<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XV.|ACCORDING TO S. MATTHEVV.|41}}</noinclude>{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XV.}}}}}}

{{c|''The Pharisees of Hierusalem comming so farre to carpe him, he chargeth with a tradition contrarie to Gods commaundement. 10 And to the people he yeldeth the reason of that which they reproued: 15 and againe to his Disciples, shewing the ground of the Pharisaical washing (to witte, that meates otherwise defile the soule) to be false. 21 then he goeth aside to hide him self among the Gentils: where, in a woman he findeth such faith, that he is faine, lest the Gentils should before the time extort the whole bread, as she had a crumme, to returne to the Iewes. 34 where (al contrarie to those Pharisees) the common people seeke wonderfully vnto him. and he after he hath cured their diseased, feedeth 4000 of them with seuen loaues.''}} {{verse|chapter=15|verse=1}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō wensday the 3. weeke in Lent.}}THEN came to him from Hierusalem Scribes and Pharisees, saying,{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 7, 1.''}} {{verse|chapter=15|verse=2}}† VVhy do thy Disciples transgresse the tradition of the Auncientes? For they wash not their hands when they eate bread. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=3}}† But he answering said to them: Why do you also transgresse the commaundement of God for your tradition? For God said, {{verse|chapter=15|verse=4}}† ''Honour father and mother''. and, ''He that shal curse father or mother, dying let him dye''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 20, 12.''}}{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Leu. 20, 9.''}} {{verse|chapter=15|verse=5}}† But you say, Whosoeuer shal say to father or mother, The gift vvhatsoeuer procedeth from me, shal profite the: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=6}}† and shal not honour his father or his mother: and you haue made frustrate the commaundement of God for your ovvne tradition. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=7}}† Hypocrites, vvel hath Esay Prophecied of you, saying, {{verse|chapter=15|verse=8}}† ''This people honoureth me ‖ vvith their lippes: but their hart is farre from me''.{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 29, 13.''}} {{verse|chapter=15|verse=9}}† ''And in vaine do they vvorshippe me, teaching doctrines and ‖ commaundements of men''.

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=10}}† And hauing called together the multitudes vnto him, he said to them, Heare ye and vnderstand. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=11}}† ‖ Not that vvhich entreth into the mouth, defileth a man: but that vvhich procedeth out of the mouth, that defileth a man. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=12}}† Then came his Disciples, and said to him, Doest thou knovv that the Pharisees, when they heard this vvord, vvere scandalized? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=13}}† But he ansvvering sayd: All planting vvhich my heauenly father hath not planted, shal be rooted vp. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=14}}† Let them alone: blinde they are, guides of the blinde. And if the blinde be guide to the blinde, both fall into the ditch. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=15}}† And Peter answering sayd to him, Expound vs this parable. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=16}}† But he sayd, Are you also as yet vvithout vnderstanding? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=17}}† Do you not vnderstand, that al that entreth into the mouth, goeth into the belly, and is cast forth into the priuy? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=18}}† But the things that proceede out of the mouth, come forth from the hart, and those things ‖ defile a man. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=19}}† For from the hart come forth euil cogitations, murders, aduoutries, fornications, thefts, false testimonies, blasphemies. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=20}}† These are the things that<noinclude>{{rh||F|defile}}</noinclude>
